anchors.reason: The candidate paper describes a different, specific dataset (FACED) and is not the data paper for EmoEEG-MC, though both are related to EEG emotion decoding.

anchors.paper_venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
anchors.reason: The paper 'Bodily maps of emotions' discusses somatosensory maps of emotions, which is topically related to EEG emotion decoding but does not describe or introduce the EmoEEG-MC dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG (64-channel) and peripheral physiological data (PPG, GSR) were recorded from 60 participants during two experimental contexts: video-induced and imagery-induced emotion elicitation, covering seven emotion categories. Subjective reports were used to validate the emotional experience for each category. Some participants have incomplete trial sets due to missing imagery or video trials.

citation_details.title: A Multi-Context Emotional EEG Dataset for Cross-Context Emotion Decoding
citation_details.author: Xin Xu, Xinke Shen, X Chen, Qingzhu Zhang, Sitian Wang, Yihan Li, Zongsheng Li, Dan Zhang, Mingming Zhang, Quanying Liu
citation_details.abstract: EEG-based emotion decoding is essential for unveiling neural mechanisms of emotion and has applications in mental health and human-machine interaction. However, existing datasets for EEG-based emotion decoding are limited to a single context of emotion elicitation. The ability of emotion decoding methods to generalize across different contexts remains underexplored. To address this gap, we present the Multi-Context Emotional EEG (EmoEEG-MC) dataset, featuring 64-channel EEG and peripheral physiological data from 60 participants exposed to two distinct contexts: video-induced and imagery-induced emotions. These contexts evoke seven distinct emotional categories: joy, inspiration, tenderness, fear, disgust, sadness, and neutral emotion. The emotional experience of specific emotion categories was validated through subjective reports. To validate the potential of cross-context emotion decoding, we implemented a support vector machine with L1 regularization, achieving accuracies of 66.7% for binary classification (positive vs. negative emotions) and 28.9% for seven-category emotion classification, both significantly above chance levels. The EmoEEG-MC dataset serves as a foundational resource for understanding the neural substrates of emotion and enhancing the real-world applicability of affective computing.

citation_details.title: Consciousness as OS and Applications: From Neural Primitive (Density × MA) to Higher-Order Emotions, Identity Formation, and Collective Cohesion
citation_details.author: 仁定 五十嵐
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: Description This deposit provides the complete computational materials for Supplement S2 of the paper “Consciousness as OS and Applications” (v2.0, April 23, 2026). Contents • Core engine: DensityMA_OS_HigherOrderEmotions_Full_Integration_Final.py • 17 standalone Python simulation scripts (simulation_01_EmoEEG_MC.py 〜 simulation_17_extreme_physiological_states.py) • Generated high-resolution result graphs (PNG, 300 dpi) for each condition • Full Supplement S2 PDF and main paper PDF The simulations test the robustness of the zero-distance self-embrace loop (nostalgia repair, intentional divergence at the Edge of Chaos, identity shake detection, and Relation_MA dynamics) on top of the Density × MA OS layer. Seventeen diverse synthetic conditions are included, inspired by real neuroimaging datasets (ds005540 EmoEEG-MC, ds003751 DENS, ds007537 smartphone, psilocybin ds006072, TMS-EEG, joint musical hyperscanning, NDE-like surge, end-of-life decline, birth/sexual intimacy/acute illness, etc.). All simulations respect the brain’s ~20 W energy constraint through continuous gradient switching among GNWT, FEP, and IIT applications. Results consistently show Relation_MA stably remains in the ideal range 2.0–2.8 across all conditions, providing direct computational evidence for the paper’s central claim: humans cannot discard the self without ceasing to exist.
